title: Electronic structure of a persistent excitonic fluid far beyond the Mott limit
authors: Weiyan Qi, Stefano Ponzoni, Ashim Pramanik, Vitaly Gorelov, Yannis Laplace, Gianluca Stefanucci, Enrico Perfetto, Esteban Morcos, Marino Marsi, Steven Francis Udaundo, Sebastian Maherlein, Amina Taleb-Ibrahimi, Kaibo Zheng, Tonu Pullerits, Luca Perfetti
abstract: Excitons are conventionally expected to destabilize at high photoexcitation densities, as screening weakens the electron-hole attraction. Recent studies, however, challenge this paradigm, suggesting that excitons generated by strong optical pumping can remain stable even beyond the onset of population inversion. Here, using time- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy on 2D hybrid perovskites, we provide direct evidence for such a high-density excitonic state, characterized by a distinctive Mexican-hat dispersion. Remarkably, this excitonic band reconstruction endures for orders of magnitude longer than the optical coherence time, revealing a population-sustained electronic structure that survives well into the incoherent regime. The excitonic resonance also persists far beyond optical saturation, at densities where exciton wavefunctions strongly overlap. Our findings reveal a long-lived, high-density quantum fluid of excitons with characteristics reminiscent of a BCS condensate, an electronic structure markedly different from that of the dilute limit.
summary: This work reports experimental evidence from 2D perovskites showing that excitons remain stable and form a high-density quantum fluid even at excitation levels predicted to cause dissociation by Mott theory. By using tr-ARPES and advanced theoretical modeling, the authors characterize this fluid via a unique Mexican-hat dispersion, confirming robust, long-lived electron-hole correlations.
main_problem: The study investigates the stability and electronic structure of excitons at high photoexcitation densities, challenging the conventional Mott picture which predicts exciton dissociation due to screening.
main_result: The authors provide direct evidence for a long-lived, high-density quantum fluid of excitons, characterized by a Mexican-hat dispersion, which persists far beyond the optical saturation threshold.
method: The research combines time- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) experiments with theoretical modeling using the pseudo-Hermitian Bethe–Salpeter Hamiltonian (PH-BSH).
model_or_system: The physical system is a two-dimensional (2D) hybrid perovskite. The theoretical framework models the system using the PH-BSH, moving beyond simple approximations to describe the excitonic fluid state.
key_observables: Mexican-hat dispersion, exciton binding energy (0.18 eV), spectral weight dispersion (downward vs. upward), and the persistence of the excitonic resonance intensity.
important_parameters: High photoexcitation densities (up to $5 	imes 10^{12}/	ext{cm}^2$), fluences significantly above the optical saturation threshold, and timescales extending into the picosecond regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the PH-BSH framework and assumes that the observed persistence of the resonance indicates a stable, correlated quantum fluid state.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate tr-ARPES maps showing the evolution of the exciton resonance intensity with increasing pump fluence, and compare the observed spectral weight dispersion in the low-density gas regime versus the high-density quantum fluid regime.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical conflict with the Mott picture, presenting experimental evidence via tr-ARPES showing the persistence of the excitonic structure, and finally comparing these observations to advanced theoretical calculations using the PH-BSH.
why_interesting: The demonstration of a high-density, long-lived excitonic fluid exhibiting BCS-like characteristics in a solid-state material provides a tangible platform for studying strongly correlated quantum matter far from equilibrium.
